survey: A stylized saguaro cactus in desert sand. The ribbed trunk is a vertical column, and its base sinks into the sand with a slight depression around it, so it is planted, not floating. Two arms branch from the trunk at different heights. The left arm leaves the trunk low, bends up at a rounded elbow and ends in a domed tip. The right arm leaves higher, passes slightly in front of the trunk and also bends upward to a domed tip. Both joints blend into the trunk the way saguaro arms do. Small spine nubs run along the ribs of the trunk and both arms. A single pink flower sits on a small green base at the crown of the trunk, as a saguaro blossom does. The trunk and arms face the camera in three-quarter view and the rib lines follow each limb's curve.
